studies.Reference: Associations of long-chain ω-3 fatty acids and fish intake with endometrial cancer risk in the VITamins And Lifestyle cohort.
studies.Authors: Brasky TM, Neuhouser ML, Cohn DE, White E
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: intakes of long-chain ω-3 PUFAs, including eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 20:5ω-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; 22:6ω-3), from diet and supplements

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 22,494 women aged 50-76 y, living in western Washington State, were recruited
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Women in the highest compared with the lowest quintile of dietary EPA + DHA intake had a 79% increased risk
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Incident endometrial cancers (n = 263) were identified through the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results cancer registry after 9 y of follow-up.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: intakes of long-chain ω-3 PUFAs, including eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA; 20:5ω-3) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; 22:6ω-3), from diet and supplements

studies.Reference: Omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acid intakes and endometrial cancer risk in a population-based case-control study.
studies.Authors: Arem H, Neuhouser ML, Irwin ML, Cartmel B, Lu L, Risch H, Mayne ST, Yu H
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Fish oil supplement use was significantly associated with reduced risk of endometrial cancer.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 556 incident cancer cases and 533 age-matched controls
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Fish oil supplement use was significantly associated with reduced risk of endometrial cancer: OR = 0.63 (95 % CI: 0.45-0.88).

studies.Reference: Long-chain ω-3 fatty acid intake and endometrial cancer risk in the Women's Health Initiative.
studies.Authors: Brasky TM, Rodabough RJ, Liu J, Kurta ML, Wise LA, Orchard TS, Cohn DE, Belury MA, White E, Manson JE, Neuhouser ML
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Stage: Type I (endometrioid) and overall endometrial cancer; main result for all types, but effect most pronounced for type I

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Women were n = 87,360 participants of the Women's Health Initiative Observational Study and Clinical Trials
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: those in the upper compared with lowest quintiles of total LCω-3PUFA intake ... had significantly reduced endometrial cancer risk (HR: 0.59; 95% CI: 0.40, 0.82; P-trend = 0.001)
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: n = 1253 incident invasive endometrial cancers were identified
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: intakes of LCω-3PUFAs ... sum of eicosapentaenoic, docosapentaenoic, and docosahexaenoic acids
